summary: The RTP/AVP profile underlies many other profiles. This document updates RFC 3551 to reflect changes in audio codec usage by removing DVI4 from the recommended codecs. The change carries through to the profiles built on RTP/AVP.

plainLanguage.summary: This update removes DVI4 from the RTP/AVP profile's minimum audio codec recommendation. It keeps PCMU as the recommended minimum codec.

subtitle: Removes DVI4 from the minimum codec recommendation in the RTP/AVP profile.

tldr.problem: Many RTP deployments did not support DVI4, despite RFC 3551 recommending it as a minimum audio codec.
tldr.mechanism: The update removes payload type 5 (DVI4) from the recommendation and retains payload type 0 (PCMU).
tldr.outcome: The change updates RFC 3551 and profiles that build on RTP/AVP.

today: RFC 7007 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3551. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 7007.

sections.title: Why the Codec Recommendation Changes
sections.content:
RFC 3551 said RTP/AVP audio applications SHOULD be able to send and receive PCMU and DVI4. The RFC notes that many deployments did not support DVI4 and that more modern codecs were available.

Because other RTP profiles build on RTP/AVP, the update also applies to those profiles by extension.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier recommendation included a codec that many deployments did not support. This RFC removes that recommendation.

sections.title: The Updated Minimum
sections.content:
The update changes the final paragraph of Section 6 of RFC 3551. It replaces the recommendation for payload types 0 (PCMU) and 5 (DVI4) with a recommendation for payload type 0 (PCMU) only.

The revised text says audio applications SHOULD be able to send and/or receive PCMU. It adds that some environments necessitate support for PCMU.
sections.plainLanguage: PCMU remains the minimum codec recommended by the profile. DVI4 is removed from that minimum recommendation.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says this change does not introduce new security considerations for RFC 3551.

It updates RFC 3551, which is the basis for RTP/AVP and the profiles named in the abstract.
sections.plainLanguage: The codec recommendation changes, but the RFC adds no security considerations.
